title: Petrarch Financial - Renewal & APAC burst capacity planning
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in focused on adding burst capacity in APAC, evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted for peak trading windows, clarifying contract term extension and SOC2/KMS requirements. Agreed to run a 72-hour latency/cost benchmark on proposed config and share pricing amendment for a 12-month extension.
topics: Contract term extension and pricing amendment
Onboarding timeline and change freeze windows
next_steps: Redwood to share amended pricing and 12-month SOW by 2027-04-01
Run 72-hour benchmark with Petrarch traffic profile starting 2027-04-05
Customer to provide sample traffic profile and peak hour slices by 2027-03-31
Schedule follow-up demo of Dedicated autoscaling controls w/ Priya week of 2027-04-06
action_items: Jordan Kim - Send pricing amendment and SOW - 2027-04-01
Daniel Chen - Provide 3 days of anonymized peak traffic + p95 latency targets - 2027-03-31
Priya Nair - Prepare benchmark harness + suggested Redwood Dedicated config - 2027-04-03
Marta Ruiz - Confirm maintenance windows and change freeze dates - 2027-04-02
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-03-29
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (AE), Priya Nair (SE), Sanjay Rao (CSM) — Petrarch: Liam O'Shea, Marta Ruiz, Daniel Chen, Asha Patel
Links shared: Pricing deck: https://app.redwood.com/decks/petrarch-renewal-v2 , Benchmark template: https://redwood.sheets/benchmarks/petrarch

[00:00] Jordan Kim: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um we'll kick off — quick roll call?
[00:12] Liam O'Shea: Liam here, hi.
[00:13] Marta Ruiz: Marta here.
[00:15] Daniel Chen: Daniel on the call.
[00:17] Asha Patel: Asha, procurement.
[00:20] Jordan Kim: awesome. quick agenda — renewal recap, APAC burst ask, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, security check, next steps. goal is to line up the bench run and pricing.

[00:45] Priya Nair: hi team, Priya, I'll mostly run through the performance pieces, proposed Dedicated config for your peak windows and how the autoscaling burst would behave.

[01:18] Liam O'Shea: great. to set context, our Q3 trading release increases conversational checks during APAC morning by about 3.5x. need to make sure we don't hit 99th percentile latency spikes. don't want to overcommit on month-to-month cost either.

[01:50] Jordan Kim: yup — makes total sense. can you remind us of the p95 and p99 numbers you're targeting during those windows?

[02:05] Daniel Chen: target p95 60ms for generation token time, p99 less than 220ms end-to-end. those are from current on-prem probe, but CPU and network vary.

[02:28] Priya Nair: ok those are helpful. quick note: when we say p95 60ms that's dependent on model and seq length; are you on the smaller Llama-based model or running a mix that includes longer-context models?

[02:45] Marta Ruiz: primarily the lighter models for inference but we do have occasional long context sessions for compliance checks. most traffic is short form.

[03:05] Priya Nair: perfect. so proposed approach — keep your baseline on Hosted for normal traffic, add Redwood Dedicated reserved pool for a 3-hour APAC morning burst. Dedicated gives the predictable throughput and lower tail latency. we can pair that with prefix KV caching to reduce re-compute on repeats.

[03:40] Liam O'Shea: sounds right — question is cost delta. can you ballpark the incremental $/token or $/hour for that burst?

[03:55] Jordan Kim: ballpark — depends on GPU type and quantization profile. for a T4-equivalent mix we estimated roughly a 1.8x unit cost during burst vs baseline hosted flexible. but per-token can drop if prefix cache hit rates are high. we'll put exact numbers in the amendment.

[04:28] Asha Patel: procurement: are there minimum commitments if we go Dedicated? we prefer a 12-month extension but want a clause for seasonal scale-down.

[04:45] Sanjay Rao: you can structure a 12-month reserved capacity with burst buffers and a seasonal adjustment clause — we've done that. the amendment will show committed baseline and pre-negotiated burst rates.

[05:10] Marta Ruiz: on security, we need SOC2 Type II artifacts, audit logs, SSO SAML, and KMS integration for key rotation. also data residency for EU (not a blocker) but APAC logs should stay in region.

[05:35] Jordan Kim: noted — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and VPC, and we can enable cross-region retention rules. we'll attach SOC2 package; Priya can call out the audit log retention options.

[06:05] Priya Nair: yeah, quick caveat — audit log retention and nearline queries add storage cost but we'll map that in the SOW. also want to flag that when you do on-prem or Private, we sometimes see slightly higher tail latency because of network egress; we'll capture that in the bench.

[06:30] Daniel Chen: understood. the bench is key — we want real traffic shape. Jordan, can you run the benchmark with our profile?

[06:40] Jordan Kim: yes, action item — we'll run 72-hour benchmark using your anonymized traffic profile. Priya will prepare the harness and exact config for the Dedicated pool and for Hosted-to-Dedicated routing to compare.

[07:05] Priya Nair: for the harness we'll include sequence-length buckets, cold-start ratios, and KV-cache hit/miss scenarios. we'll also simulate failover to Hosted to validate graceful degradation — that's important for SLAs.

[07:40] Liam O'Shea: perf aside, can you walk through the autoscaling behavior? during a burst do VMs spin up quickly enough — we need <2min ramp ideally.

[07:55] Priya Nair: Dedicated autoscaling is node-based with reserved capacity. the ramp depends on reserved buffer and warm pool. we recommend keeping a warm reserve for those 3 peak hours which gives sub-60s token-generation ramp for most requests. full node provisioning can take longer, but warm-pools are instant.

[08:25] Marta Ruiz: what's the warm-pool cost?

[08:30] Jordan Kim: warm-pool is charged at a lower standby rate; we will show numbers in the amendment. again hit rates and caching reduce total token compute.

[09:05] Asha Patel: hypothetically if NimbusAI offers an always-on cheaper option for APAC, why should we pick Redwood Dedicated?

[09:18] Jordan Kim: good question — big differentiator is tooling and observability. Redwood Console gives token-level cost breakdowns, per-route tracing and automatic fallback policies. also our model catalog optimizes kernels per hardware which tends to improve tail latency for mixed sequence workloads. plus we have a predictable SOW for burst windows.

[09:50] Daniel Chen: any known gotchas when moving from Hosted to Dedicated mid-quarter? downtime?

[10:00] Priya Nair: no planned downtime; routing switch is seamless, but you'll need to test session affinity and KV cache warming. that's why the benchmark run will include failover tests.

[10:30] Jordan Kim: ok turning to timeline — if we get the traffic profile by 2027-03-31 we'll run bench 2027-04-05 to 2027-04-08, and then deliver results + pricing by 2027-04-12. does that align?

[10:45] Liam O'Shea: yes that timeline works.

[11:05] Marta Ruiz: maintenance windows — we have a change freeze 2027-04-15 to 2027-04-22 for the trading release; can't have infra changes then.

[11:20] Sanjay Rao: we'll respect the freeze and target earlier dates for any config flips.

[11:40] Jordan Kim: quick note on observability — we'll enable per-model dashboards and token cost breakdowns for your finance team. also can export JSON logs into your SIEM.

[12:05] Daniel Chen: cool. also want to validate KV caching won't surface stale PII data — what's the TTL and encryption model?

[12:20] Priya Nair: KV cache uses customer-level namespace, TTL configurable, and all cache entries are encrypted at rest via KMS. we can show config options in the security packet.

[12:50] Asha Patel: procurement question — if we commit 12 months and seasonally downscale, is there a credit or reconciliation process?

[13:05] Sanjay Rao: yes we can include a seasonal reconciliation clause where actual usage vs committed baseline is reconciled quarterly with pro-rata credits. details in SOW.

[13:30] Liam O'Shea: okay good. any blockers on our side? we need the bench template and a small script to scrub traffic — who owns that?

[13:42] Daniel Chen: we can anonymize and hand it off, but want Redwood to validate scrubbing.

[13:50] Priya Nair: we'll provide the scrubbing checklist and scaffold script. you'll run locally and then upload sanitized traces to the harness.

[14:15] Jordan Kim: wrapping up — quick recap: Redwood will send pricing amendment + SOW by 2027-04-01; Petrarch provides traffic profile by 2027-03-31; Redwood runs 72-hour bench 2027-04-05 to 2027-04-08; follow-up demo of Dedicated autoscaling w/ Priya week of 2027-04-06.

[14:50] Marta Ruiz: sounds good. one last ask: can you include a short rollback playbook if we see unexpected latency during the release window?

[15:05] Priya Nair: yes we'll draft a rollback playbook and include warm-pool fallback and immediate routing to Hosted.

[15:20] Asha Patel: procurement will review SOW; expect internal legal review 5-7 business days after we get amendment.

[15:35] Jordan Kim: perfect. thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with links and the action items.

[15:50] Liam O'Shea: thanks all.

[16:00] Meeting close.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional speaker overlap, a few product names transcribed as "KV cash" or "K V cache"; timestamps approximate.
